text: Launch on-demand GPU clusters from 16 up to 512+ GPUs, or start with a single node, no long-term commitment
quote: Launch 16x to 512x NVIDIA H100 or B200 GPU clusters instantly, or start with a single-node instance. No long-term commitments.

text: Production-ready clusters scale from 16 to 2,000+ NVIDIA B200 or H100 GPUs

text: 1-Click Clusters combine GPU and CPU nodes with GPUDirect RDMA interconnect up to 3200 Gb/s
quote: 1-Click Clusters (1CC) are high-performance clusters composed of both GPU and CPU nodes, featuring 16 to 512 NVIDIA H100 or B200 SXM Tensor Core GPUs...enabling peer-to-peer GPUDirect RDMA at up to 3200 Gb/s

text: Quick start guide takes you from SSH access to running a first multi-node GPU job in minutes
quote: The quick start takes you from SSH to your first multi-node GPU job in minutes.

text: Clusters can be run with Managed Kubernetes, Preinstalled Kubernetes, or Slurm scheduler
quote: Launch 16x to 512x NVIDIA H100 or B200 GPU clusters instantly, or start with a single-node instance. No long-term commitments. Choose from Managed Kubernetes, Preinstalled Kubernetes, or Slurm.

text: Managed Kubernetes (MK8s) offers GPU and InfiniBand/RDMA support with shared persistent storage, preconfigured for immediate use
quote: MK8s provides a Kubernetes environment with GPU and InfiniBand (RDMA) support, and shared persistent storage across all nodes in a 1CC. Clusters are preconfigured so you can deploy workloads without additional setup.

text: Slurm automatically schedules workloads to maximize cluster utilization and avoid resource contention
quote: Slurm automatically schedules workloads, maximizing cluster utilization while preventing resource contention.

text: Lambda actively monitors and maintains health of Slurm control daemons (slurmctld, slurmdbd)
quote: Lambda monitors and maintains the health of Slurm daemons such as slurmctld and slurmdbd.

text: Guides walk through deploying a vLLM inference server on the cluster with a Kubernetes Service and Ingress
quote: you'll deploy a vLLM server to serve the Nous Research Hermes 4 model. You'll: Create a namespace... Deploy the vLLM server. Expose it with a Service. Configure an Ingress to make it accessible externally.

text: Instances come with Lambda Stack preinstalled: a standard set of AI/ML drivers, tools, and frameworks
quote: Lambda also preinstalls Lambda Stack, a standard set of AI/ML-related drivers, tools, and frameworks, on the instance

text: A minimal 'GPU Base' Ubuntu image is available for users who want full control over their Python environment
quote: GPU Base: An image based on Ubuntu Server that includes a minimal set of key AI/ML tools and drivers... Use if: You want a minimal working setup with a high degree of control over your Python environment.

text: Cluster nodes come with Open MPI, CUDA, Podman, Apptainer, Pyxis, and Enroot preinstalled
quote: Container and HPC software: Open MPI, CUDA, Podman, Apptainer, Pyxis, and Enroot are preinstalled.

text: Each on-demand instance includes a preinstalled JupyterLab server for creating and managing notebooks
quote: each ODC instance provides a JupyterLab installation for creating and managing Jupyter notebooks

text: You can connect to instances directly via SSH or through the preinstalled JupyterLab server
quote: You can connect to your On-Demand Cloud (ODC) instances directly through SSH or by using the preinstalled JupyterLab server.

text: Instances can be launched programmatically via the Lambda Cloud API
quote: You can also launch instances programmatically by using the Lambda Cloud API.

text: The Lambda Cloud API exposes REST endpoints to create and manage cloud resources
quote: The Lambda Cloud API provides a set of REST API endpoints you can use to create and manage your Lambda Cloud resources.

text: When launching via the API, you can supply cloud-init instructions for launch-time configuration
quote: you can add launch-time configuration instructions using [cloud-init]

text: The API lets you choose an alternative/custom base image for your instance instead of the default
quote: the API allows you to use a different base image for your instance

text: 1-Click Clusters feature 16 to 512 NVIDIA H100 or B200 SXM GPUs across GPU and CPU nodes
quote: 1-Click Clusters (1CC) are high-performance clusters composed of both GPU and CPU nodes, featuring 16 to 512 NVIDIA H100 or B200 SXM Tensor Core GPUs.

text: A high-capacity regional filesystem (up to 8 EB) can be attached to instances to store datasets and back up system state
quote: A filesystem is a high-capacity regional file store you can attach to your instance to store datasets and back up system state. In most regions, each filesystem has a capacity of 8 EB

text: A shared /home filesystem provides a consistent environment (scripts, venvs, checkpoints) across all cluster nodes
quote: Shared /home filesystem: Provides a consistent user environment across all nodes, for example, personal scripts, virtual environments, and model checkpoints.

text: Instances are billed hourly but in one-minute increments
quote: ODC prices instances by hourly usage and bills in one-minute increments.

text: Firewall rules on the Firewall page let you restrict incoming traffic to instances and cluster head nodes
quote: You can restrict incoming traffic to the instances in a workspace, including 1-Click Cluster management (head) nodes, by creating firewall rules on the Firewall page

text: Lambda provides support according to agreed service-level agreements
quote: Lambda provides support according to the service level agreements (SLAs) in place with the customer.

text: On-Demand Cloud provides on-demand Linux GPU virtual machine instances
quote: On-Demand Cloud (ODC) provides on-demand access to Linux-based, GPU-backed virtual machine instances.

text: Private Cloud offers single-tenant clusters of 1,000+ GPUs with low-level infrastructure access
quote: Private Cloud is the ideal solution for organizations requiring a single-tenant cluster with 1,000+ GPUs. Private Cloud customers have low-level access to their cluster infrastructure.

text: Monthly instance usage can be viewed on the Usage page's Instances tab
quote: To view your monthly usage, navigate to the [Usage page]...and then click the **Instances** tab.

text: On-Demand Cloud offers a range of instance types including HGX B200, GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip, and H100 GPUs
quote: ODC offers a variety of predefined instance types to support different workload requirements. Available GPUs include the state-of-the-art NVIDIA HGX B200 GPU, NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip, and NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU

text: S3-compatible tools like rclone and s5cmd can be used to copy files to/from Lambda filesystems
quote: This adapter allows you to use S3-compatible tools like rclone and s5cmd to copy files to and from your filesystems and perform common file operations.

text: GPU usage can be monitored via an NVIDIA DCGM Grafana dashboard
quote: Monitor GPU usage with the NVIDIA DCGM Grafana dashboard.

text: Self-serve, first-come deployment of B200, H100, A100, or GH200 instances in minutes
quote: Deploy NVIDIA B200, H100, A100, or GH200 instances in minutes with self-serve, first-come access.

text: Lmod lets users dynamically load/unload software modules (e.g. HPC-X, Node.js, uv) on the cluster
quote: Lmod for environment management: Use Lmod to dynamically load and unload software modules available on the cluster, such as HPC-X, Node.js, and uv.

text: Reserved capacity pricing is available for sustained usage at the lowest rates
quote: Contact us for reserved capacity at our lowest prices.
